cards.headline: The opener came from a 2004 album under another name
cards.snippet: "La Vita" comes from Primal Prayer, a 2004 album Beverly Glenn-Copeland released under the alias Phynix after rebounding from a health scare. Pitchfork notes that it opens the 2020 compilation Transmissions with operatic Italian before melting into "Ever New."
cards.context: Transmissions (2020) is a career-spanning compilation on Transgressive.

cards.headline: The New Yorker heard homemade early-90s world-beat
cards.snippet: Reviewing the 2020 compilation Transmissions, The New Yorker singled out the lyric "My mother says to me / Enjoy your life" in "La Vita." It said the track sounds like a homemade take on early-nineties world-beat dance music.
cards.context: The lyric is the hook that many commenters connect with their own mothers.

cards.headline: Thirty years of silence, then "Send me 30 of them"
cards.snippet: Glenn Copeland's music sat largely unknown for decades. Then, around 2015, a collector in Japan emailed asking whether he had an old cassette called Keyboard Fantasies, and asked him to send 30 copies. Copeland was stunned, since nobody had asked for anything in about 30 years. The email launched the late-career revival that brought songs like this to wider ears.
cards.context: The collector, Ryota Masuko, reached out in 2015.

cards.headline: A stranger's grief, answered by a song
cards.snippet: I'm dealing with the loss of a wonderful mum, coping with the changes to life that her death has brought, and I hear your song. Every word could have been written for me.
cards.context: The song's mother-themed lyric lands hard for people grieving.

cards.headline: Runway discovery
cards.snippet: I just heard this on Balmain runway and I’m OBSESSED
cards.context: Several commenters found the song through fashion shows, including Balmain and Dior.
